title: Question 1.7
statement_text: Let $t\geq 6$ be an integer. Does there exist a graph $G$ with $E(\overline{G})\neq\varnothing$ such that $G$ is $C_{2t-2}$-free but $G+e$ has an induced subgraph isomorphic to $C_{2t-2}$ for every $e\in E(\overline{G})$?
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $\overline{G}$ is the complement of $G$, $G-e$ removes an edge $e\in E(G)$ and $G+e$ adds a non-edge $e\in E(\overline{G})$. $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$, and $G$ is $H$-induced-saturated if $G$ is $H$-free, $G-e$ contains an induced $H$ for every $e\in E(G)$, and $G+e$ contains an induced $H$ for every $e\in E(\overline{G})$. $C_t$ is the cycle on $t$ vertices. For paths, $P_t$-induced-saturated graphs exist iff $t\notin\{1,4\}$ (Martin–Smith, Bonamy et al., Dvořák). For odd cycles, the line graph of $K_{t,t}$ is $C_{2t-1}$-induced-saturated (Behrens et al.). For even cycles, examples are known only for $C_4$ (icosahedron), $C_6$ ($C_5\square C_5$), $C_8$ (dodecahedron) and $C_{10}$ (a 28-vertex graph found by computer); existence is wide open for even cycles on 12 or more vertices. The authors prove the 'removal half': for every $t\ge5$ there is a graph $G_t$ with at least one edge that is $C_{2t-2}$-free but such that $G_t-e$ has an induced $C_{2t-2}$ for every edge $e$. This question asks for the other half, the edge-addition condition, which the authors see as a good start towards extending their methods to the full induced saturation problem for long even cycles. In the paper the question is written with '$H$-free'; from the context $H$ is the cycle $C_{2t-2}$.
paper_title: Halfway to induced saturation for even cycles

title: Question 1.8
statement_text: Does there exist a polynomial $f$ such that for every $t\geq 3$, there is a graph $G$ on at most $f(t)$ vertices with $E(G)\neq\varnothing$, such that $G$ is $C_{2t-2}$-free but $G-e$ has an induced subgraph isomorphic to $C_{2t-2}$ for every $e\in E(G)$?
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $\overline{G}$ is the complement of $G$, $G-e$ removes an edge $e\in E(G)$ and $G+e$ adds a non-edge $e\in E(\overline{G})$. $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$, and $G$ is $H$-induced-saturated if $G$ is $H$-free, $G-e$ contains an induced $H$ for every $e\in E(G)$, and $G+e$ contains an induced $H$ for every $e\in E(\overline{G})$. $C_t$ is the cycle on $t$ vertices. For paths, $P_t$-induced-saturated graphs exist iff $t\notin\{1,4\}$ (Martin–Smith, Bonamy et al., Dvořák). For odd cycles, the line graph of $K_{t,t}$ is $C_{2t-1}$-induced-saturated (Behrens et al.). For even cycles, examples are known only for $C_4$ (icosahedron), $C_6$ ($C_5\square C_5$), $C_8$ (dodecahedron) and $C_{10}$ (a 28-vertex graph found by computer); existence is wide open for even cycles on 12 or more vertices. The authors prove the 'removal half': for every $t\ge5$ there is a graph $G_t$ with at least one edge that is $C_{2t-2}$-free but such that $G_t-e$ has an induced $C_{2t-2}$ for every edge $e$. The graphs $G_t$ constructed by the authors have a number of vertices doubly exponential in $t$, and they do not even know a reason to expect more than linearly many vertices to be needed; this question asks whether polynomially many suffice. In the paper the question is written with '$H$-free'; from the context $H$ is the cycle $C_{2t-2}$.
paper_title: Halfway to induced saturation for even cycles
